title: Planar simple random walk non-return probability and expected range
source_title: Some Problems on Random Walk in Space
source_version: University of California Press, Second Berkeley Symposium proceedings, 1951, printed pp. 353–367, 15-page Rényi archive scan

work_ref.source_version: University of California Press, Second Berkeley Symposium proceedings, 1951, printed pp. 353–367, 15-page Rényi archive scan

difficulty_reason: After the elementary on-diagonal return estimate is given, the authors build the exact last-return renewal identity, split it at a moving truncation k=m−floor(m/log m) and extract matching planar non-return bounds, then connect them to the expected range by reversal and summation.
selected_claim: For nearest-neighbor simple random walk on Z², the probability of no return in the first k steps is of order 1/log k, and the expected range after t steps is of order t/log t. The author paper actually gives leading constant π. Its γ₂(n) indexes n−1 steps and its L₂(n) omits S₂(0); these shifts preserve the exact exercise order. No other dimension or range moments are counted.

statement_spans.label: Planar non-return estimate (2.18), expected range in Theorem 1 equation (2.20); precise scope is d=2.

proof_spans.label: Section 2 γ_d(n) increment reversal and last-return identity (2.5)–(2.6), with parity and return estimate.
Planar lower and upper bounds (2.11)–(2.15), refined estimate (2.18) and first-moment identity (2.19) through the planar clause (2.20).

context_spans.label: Original planar nearest-neighbor walk, independence and exact range convention.

source_caveats: Physical p4 prints k≤2n in an intermediate factorial sum whose denominator contains (n−k)!. The same author display gives the binomial-square closed form. The exercise orders and leading constant already use (2.4) and (2.11)–(2.15), with (2.19). Preserve original print.
